text:
The evidence can't confirm that timber harvest caused the loss.

What it shows: Hansen/UMD mapped about 81.3 ha of tree-cover loss in 2021 within the asset (2.23% of its area). The result is corroborated: JRC 2020 forest data agrees on 98% of the affected area, and later years were observed. The national forest map classes 68.1 ha of the loss as planted forest (Pinus elliottii and Pinus taeda). The other 13.2 ha is outside mapped forest, and none is native forest. A further 37.3 ha of loss in patches under 0.5 ha was not counted as an event.

So the loss is mostly in pine plantation, which is consistent with harvest. But that is context, not cause. Hansen loss captures any stand replacement, including cutting, fire or storm damage, and the tools don't identify which occurred. The evidence also says nothing about legality, responsibility or compliance.

To confirm harvest, you would need harvest records, permits or higher-resolution imagery showing the pattern and any replanting.
